title: Two improvements merged; they work after you update sage

blocks.label: Where this is
blocks.text: Release 1.0 › two single tasks from your request of 7 Nov for fewer restrictions › both merged on 10 Nov

head: Piece of work
What changes for you
How I know it works
Cost
You must act
rows: Leads wait for the automatic checks before reviews
No review starts on a commit whose checks failed, so no tokens go to reviews of a broken commit. A lead also briefs a framed task itself.
One clean cycle on the final commit: code review clean, QA pass, checks pass.
0.6 M tokens, about 1 h of agent time (measured)
The chief cleans up the folders that agents leave
The chief removes the leftover folders in your worktrees folder, and saves its own pages, without asking you. A task worktree stays: only git can remove it, and git refuses one with changes.
The first review found that the chief could delete a live task folder. One repair round fixed it and two small findings. Then one clean cycle: code review clean, QA pass, checks pass.
1.4 M tokens, about 2.5 h of agent time (measured)

blocks.label: What I did not check
blocks.text: How many review tokens the wait saves; that needs a week of runs after your update. I did not see either change in a live session, because your sessions run the older sage.

blocks.label: Weak points
blocks.text: Seven small findings stay on the polish list of the clean-up change. For example, git's forced remove still runs when its option name is shortened.

blocks.label: What you need to do
blocks.text: Update sage in Claude Code and in Codex, and start new sessions. Until you do, your sessions run the older sage.
